name: Lumaril
summary: Lumaril develops intelligence software for the physical economy, where industrial activity and operating conditions are difficult to observe in real time.
overview: Lumaril builds an intelligence layer for physical production. It connects to existing industrial control systems, learns operating conditions and uses control methods, AI and machine learning to optimize throughput, yield and reliability.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: No confirmed priced financing was located during this profile update.

bull_case: If Lumaril can demonstrate repeatable yield and throughput improvements without replacing a customer's control stack, it can capture value in capital-intensive industrial operations.
bear_case: Industrial deployment cycles are long, integrations are demanding and autonomous changes to production systems must clear a high safety and reliability bar.
directory_notes: The company has limited public financial disclosure, making product traction and funding confirmation the relevant next milestones.

intelligence.location: New York and El Segundo, California
intelligence.description: Industrial-intelligence software that connects to existing control systems to improve plant operations.
company: Lumaril connects to existing control systems in industrial facilities and builds a live model of operations. It says its software can adjust set points, control logic and coordination to improve output and yield.

Its stated target customers are complex, capital-intensive operations, including manufacturing, chemicals, biologics, oil and gas. The company has not publicly disclosed a priced financing or valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Industrial AI can create value through operational improvement rather than pure knowledge-work automation. The important proof points are verified customer outcomes, safe deployment and the time required to integrate into plant workflows.

changed.text: Profile reviewed against available public information.

takeaways: Lumaril targets throughput, yield and reliability in existing industrial facilities.
Its approach connects to current control systems rather than requiring a full replacement stack.
No public valuation is asserted without a confirmed priced transaction.
The next useful evidence will be product adoption, financing, and operating disclosure.
